common_name: White Profusion Butterfly Bush (Classic Pure White Buddleja)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; cut back hard in late winter to about 12 inches to encourage vigorous new flowering growth. White Profusion bears large, pure white flower spikes with a small yellow eye.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; cut back hard to about 12 inches in late winter to encourage vigorous, floriferous new growth. White Profusion produces long, dense, pure white flower spikes with a small golden-yellow eye at each floret, opening on a vigorous, large-growing shrub through summer into fall. Its clean white color makes it a versatile choice for a moon garden or as a bright contrast against darker-leaved shrubs, and like all buddleja it draws butterflies and hummingbirds in large numbers once established. It tolerates heat and drought well once its root system is established, needing little care beyond the annual hard cutback.
sources: North Carolina State University JC Raulston Arboretum

common_name: Montrose Purple Chaste Tree (Deep Purple-Flowered Vitex Selection)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained soil in full sun; Montrose Purple bears deeper purple flower spikes than most other chaste tree selections.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container specimens in well-drained, average to poor soil in full sun. Montrose Purple bears notably deeper, richer purple flower spikes than most other chaste tree selections, standing out from the more common lavender-blue tones typical of the species, on a vigorous shrub or small tree that blooms profusely on new growth from summer through fall. It tolerates the heat, drought, and poor soil that defeat many other flowering shrubs, and the fragrant, gray-green palmately compound foliage adds a pleasant sage-like scent to the garden. Cutting back hard in late winter to 12-18 inches above ground produces vigorous new growth and the best flower display, and it is a favorite of bees and butterflies through its long bloom season.
